sara-sales: Hey team — POC with ByteWave. Stress test at ~220 concurrent users, their harness sees intermittent 429s around 1:12pm PST. They say it happens after a burst of quick chat completions. Can eng help triage?

alex-eng: Thanks Sara. Can you grab one of the failing request IDs from the client logs? We need request_id + route (e.g. /v1/generate-chat) and the X-Redwood-Quota-* headers if present.

sara-sales: Here's one from the customer logs: request_id=rwd-zz9f3, route=/v1/chat/completions, status=429, body={"error":"rate_limited","code":429,"request_id":"rwd-zz9f3","retry_after":3}

mike-ops: I pulled telemetry for rwd-zz9f3. We see a token spike: their client sent 12 parallel calls that each used ~600 tokens within a 2s window. Our per-tenant token burst window default is 5s and per-route cap is 6k tokens/5s. They hit ~7.2k.

alex-eng: OK that explains it — token accounting (not just calls) tripped the per-route token cap. Two immediate options: 1) reduce their per-call max_tokens or batch fewer parallel calls; 2) temporary quota bump on the sales side while POC runs.

jules-ml: Also check if they mixed embeddings + chat in same tenant. Embedding jobs can be high token, and their harness does synchronous embedding prep before every chat. If they're doing that serially across many threads it magnifies token load. Recommend caching embeddings or moving embedding prep to a background worker.

sara-sales: Customer says they do an embedding call per message to rerank candidates before generating reply. They can change but want a short window while we validate.

mike-ops: I can apply a temporary per-tenant token budget bump for ByteWave for the next 48 hours. That will raise per-route cap from 6k -> 12k tokens/5s for probation. Want me to proceed?

emily-sa: Do that and also add a note to the POC runbook: "If you see repeated 429s, capture X-Redwood-Request-Id and X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining headers and ping sales@redwood with the id." Also offer them a quick config change: set max_concurrency=8 on their harness to smooth spikes.

alex-eng: For longer term: we can recommend two code changes on their side — reduce max_tokens from 600 -> 350 for fast responses, and use prefix caching for common prompts. On backend we should consider exposing a per-route smoothing flag (burst_window_ms) to sales for scheduled POCs.

ratebot: [automated] quota-bump request logged: ticket=RB-4312 assigned->mike-ops, change=per-tenant-token-cap 6k->12k window=5s duration=48h.

mike-ops: Done. Applied the 48h bump. I also added a temporary rule to allow one extra burst per minute while we monitor. I will watch metrics for the next 2 hours and post an update.

jules-ml: If you want to reproduce locally: run 12 parallel requests with max_tokens=600 and include \"n\":1; you'll see the same 429s in ~2s. Example quick test:```bash
for i in {1..12}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"max_tokens":600}' & done; wait
```

alex-eng: Thanks. After bump I'll set a short alert rule on token-usage % that pings #sales if they exceed 80% of the provisional cap. Sara, can you coordinate with ByteWave to rerun the harness in 30m and share logs if anything else pops?

sara-sales: On it. Let me know when monitoring is live. Also sending ByteWave a short checklist: 1) capture request IDs, 2) include X-Redwood-Request-Id header on logs, 3) try max_concurrency=8 and max_tokens=350.

mike-ops: Monitoring enabled. Current metrics look stable post-bump but we'll keep an eye. If we see sustained >12k/5s we'll rollback and escalate to capacity planning.

emily-sa: If this POC needs sustained high throughput, propose a short Dedicated pool trial — that avoids tenant-level caps and gives predictable throughput. I can draft pricing options for the trial.

sara-sales: Customer prefers to stay hosted for now but open to trial if this keeps recurring. I'll update them and kick off the rerun in 30m.

alex-eng: One last debugging tip — ask them to include the response headers when a 429 occurs. We return: X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining, X-Redwood-Quota-Limit, X-Redwood-Request-Id and Retry-After. Those make triage immediate.

sara-sales: Will send that checklist. Thanks everyone — I'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
